newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore urged to attract more long-term capital.
newsitem.headline: Singapore urged to attract more long-term capital.

text.p: Singapore needs to attract more long-term capital to fund the region's burgeoning infrastructure needs and maintain its competitive edge in the global financial services industry, a member of parliament said on Thursday.

Tan Soo Khoon, speaker of parliament, said Singapore's financial sector employs only five percent of the workforce but contributes almost 12 percent to gross domestic product, up from four percent in the early 1970s.
He said the short-term concentration of Singapore's financial markets was reflected in the fact that only three percent of the Asian Dollar market's liabilities have maturities longer than one year.

Citing the Asian Development Bank's estimate that Asia would invest some US$1 trillion in power, roads and telecommunications between 1994 and 2000, Tan said Singapore needed to attract long-term investment funds and their suppliers.

He said there were 135 financial institutions managing a total of Singapore $90.4 billion in the city-state at the end of 1995, but added, "The potential to grow further is huge; the world's top 20 global investment funds manage more than US$100 billion each."
